interest: Covers FBI wartime surveillance of Japanese agents in Chile, including police chief Jorge Garretón's bribery by agent Takayasu Hombo.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.20225) covers investigations and surveillance reports compiled primarily by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the U.S. Embassy in Santiago between February 1945 and April 1946 regarding Japanese intelligence, espionage, and propaganda activities in Chile and cross-border connections with Argentina. The documents examine a variety of suspected Axis operatives, commercial fronts, and associates, including Chilean Air Force Lieutenant Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote and his Dutch stepfather Barend Barends (former accountant and manager of the Japanese-controlled Compañía Chilena Oriental), former Japanese espionage contact Takayasu Hombo and his bribery of Chilean Investigaciones Director Jorge Garretón, code clerk Mitsuo Watanabe and shipping agent Kaoru Yamada, commercial agent Dennosuke Nakagawa, photographer Kyutaro Tsunekawa and the Caupolicán agricultural colony, Japanese Legation translator Isao Takeda, and an investigation into communications between German-Chilean hotelier Edwin R. Muller and Japanese agent Nobuo Ikeda in Buenos Aires. Across these investigations, U.S. intelligence sources evaluated allegations of illicit funds, diplomatic pouch abuse, subversive networks, and compliance with wartime relegation orders, often concluding that suspected subjects were either inactive or innocent of active espionage by late 1944 and 1945.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an FBI investigative report concerning Chilean Air Force Lieutenant Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote and suspected espionage during a visit to the United States.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports suspicions that Chilean Air Force Lt. Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote might spy for Japan proved unfounded; he expressed strong pro-Allied views after returning to Santiago.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting report on Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon - Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: FBI investigative report on Chilean Air Force pilot Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote, evaluating potential espionage links to his stepfather Barend Barends.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: FBI surveillance found no suspicious contacts by Lt. Toro-Mazote after his October 1944 US Lend-Lease aircraft mission; he expressed pro-Allied sentiment and no link to his suspected stepfather Barend Barends.
subfiles.title: FBI Report on Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote (Granada)

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an FBI investigative report concerning Barend Barends, a Dutch citizen in Chile suspected of dealing with Japanese elements.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards a report on Barend Barends (Spiekermann), a Dutch national in Chile with Japanese commercial ties, to the Embassy, FEA, ONI, and G-2.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting report on Barend Barends
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon - Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: Investigative memorandum on the commercial holdings, mining investments, bank accounts, and Japanese connections of Barend Barends.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: FBI memo finds no suspicious transactions by Barend Barends and discounts claims he or ex-President Juan Esteban Montero held 20,000,000 pesos in Japanese funds.
subfiles.title: FBI Memorandum on Financial Interests and Surveillance of Barend Barends

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an FBI memorandum summarizing intelligence regarding Chilean Air Force officer Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports that investigations found no evidence of subversive or espionage activity by Lt. Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote despite earlier suspicions.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting memorandum on Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon - Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an investigative report concerning Japanese national Kaoru Yamada in Chile and his alleged connection to agent Mitsuo Watanabe in Argentina.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards a report on Kaoru Yamada, an associate of Japanese agent Mitsuo Watanabe, noting Yamada was released by Chile and now lives inactively in Rengo.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting report on Kaoru Yamada and Mitsuo Watanabe
subfiles.to: Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: Investigative report on mailings sent to Japanese code clerk Mitsuo Watanabe in Buenos Aires from 550 Calle Monjitas and the background of Kaoru Yamada.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: FBI finds Kaoru Yamada, former shipping clerk at 550 Calle Monjitas, was not repatriated and now lives in Rengo with agent Takayasu Hombo, once linked to the Japanese Embassy's propaganda section.
subfiles.title: FBI Report on Mitsuo Watanabe, Kaoru Yamada, and 550 Calle Monjitas

subfiles.about: Follow-up investigative report on Chilean Air Force pilot Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote, detailing his military record, family, and pro-Allied attitudes.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Background investigation finds Lt. Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote, promoted and praised by fellow officers as pro-Allied, had no subversive ties despite a past friendship with Axis-leaning Captain Jorge Anacona.
subfiles.title: FBI Report on Lieutenant Carlos Federico Toro-Mazote (Granada)

subfiles.about: Report on Chilean national Herman Casas Cordero, detained in Costa Rica, who alleged recruitment by Japanese diplomat Nagoya Nagamine to spy in Panama.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports Herman Casas Cordero, detained in Costa Rica, claimed Japanese Legation official Nagoya Nagamine offered him money for intelligence via the Chilean diplomatic pouch.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover regarding Herman Casas Cordero and Japanese Espionage Solicitation

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an investigative memorandum concerning Barend Barends, his former employment with Compañía Chilena Oriental, and his current activities.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards a memo on Barend Barends's past Japanese commercial ties and pro-Axis sympathies, noting surveillance found no current subversive activity.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting memorandum on Barend Barends
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon - Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: Comprehensive investigative report on Barend Barends, his role at Compañía Chilena Oriental, contacts with relegated Japanese partners, and coal company finances.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive FBI report details an extensive investigation into Barend Barends, including direct interviews and statements from former colleagues. Barends recounted his work as accountant for the Japanese firm Compañía Chilena Oriental under Yonosuke Hagiwara, admitting he visited relegated partners in San Francisco de Mostazal and Melipilla to settle business matters, but strongly denied handling clandestine funds or espionage. Former cashier Luis López Pozo confirmed Barends' outspoken pro-Nazi views during early Axis victories while asserting that Japanese partners never entrusted Barends with confidential affairs. The report also details Mrs. Barends' minority holding in the CORFO-supported Compañía Carbonífera Victoria de Lebu, provides an audited balance sheet of the company, and records Dutch Consul Herman Gerhard von Oven's confirmation that Barends was blacklisted by the Dutch colony for pro-Nazi sympathies.
subfiles.title: FBI Report on Barend Barends (Spiekermann) and Commercial Affiliations

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a Legal Attaché report regarding former Japanese espionage agent Takayasu Hombo and non-enforcement of his internment order.
subfiles.from: Claude G. Bowers - U.S. Ambassador to Chile
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Bowers transmits a Legal Attaché report finding Japanese agent Takayasu Hombo currently inactive, though he evaded a 1943 relegation order by gifting a Buick to ex-police chief Jorge Garretón.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 12,671 from Claude G. Bowers transmitting Legal Attaché Report on Takayasu Hombo

subfiles.about: Legal Attaché intelligence report on Takayasu Hombo's espionage activities, bribery of police director Jorge Garretón, and financial dealings.
subfiles.from: Legal Attaché, American Embassy, Santiago, Chile
subfiles.summary: Legal Attaché report: Takayasu Hombo evaded relegation by bribing ex-Investigaciones chief Jorge Garretón with a Buick, lived off selling his store, and had lent over 250,000 pesos to a pro-Axis theater owner.
subfiles.title: Legal Attaché Report on Takayasu Hombo (Hombo)
subfiles.to: Claude G. Bowers - U.S. Ambassador to Chile

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an FBI memorandum regarding former Japanese espionage agent Takayasu Hombo in Chile.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards a memo on Takayasu Hombo, a former Japanese espionage operative in Chile now believed inactive, to Naval Intelligence and G-2.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting memorandum on Takayasu Hombo
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon - Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: FBI memorandum detailing Takayasu Hombo's espionage connections, automobile bribery of Investigaciones Director Garretón, and business dealings.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: FBI memo recounts how Takayasu Hombo avoided relegation by gifting a Buick to police chief Jorge Garretón, and had lent money to Eduardo Bahamondes Muñoz of the Axis-leaning Teatro Comedia.
subfiles.title: FBI Memorandum on Takayasu Hombo (Hombo)

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an FBI memorandum concerning Dennosuke Nakagawa, a representative of Japanese commercial firms in Chile.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards a memo on Japanese national Dennosuke Nakagawa, who represented Japanese commercial firms in Chile, to the Embassy and Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting memorandum on Dennosuke Nakagawa
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon - Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: Investigative memorandum on Dennosuke Nakagawa, his lifestyle in Melipilla, coastal travels, and response to espionage allegations.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: FBI investigation in Melipilla finds Dennosuke Nakagawa, a former commercial representative, dismissive of espionage suspicions; he vanished with an unnamed Japanese companion in September 1945.
subfiles.title: FBI Memorandum on Dennosuke Nakagawa in Melipilla

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an FBI memorandum regarding Kyutaro Tsunekawa, a Japanese photographer in Santiago suspected of subversive activity.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards a memo noting Kyutaro Tsunekawa denied any subversive activity or knowledge of Japanese espionage or sabotage in Chile.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting memorandum on Kyutaro Tsunekawa
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon - Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: Interrogation report of Kyutaro Tsunekawa regarding the Japanese Society of Santiago and the Caupolicán agricultural colony near Rengo.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: FBI finds photographer Kyutaro Tsunekawa founded a 1943 Japanese farming cooperative near Rengo that collapsed after 1945 rains ruined its sunflower-oil crop; police found no subversive record.
subfiles.title: FBI Memorandum on Kyutaro Tsunekawa (Tsunekawa Kyutaro)

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an FBI memorandum concerning Isao Takeda, former employee of the Japanese Trade Agency and Japanese Military Attaché in Santiago.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards a memo noting Isao Takeda, a secretary for the Japanese Trade Agency in Santiago, appeared involved in espionage.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting memorandum on Isao Takeda
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon - Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: Investigative report and interrogation of Isao Takeda concerning wartime diplomatic employment, bank transactions, and internment in Chile.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: FBI interview clarifies that espionage allegations against Isao Takeda actually concerned Commercial Attaché Itsuki Takada; Takeda himself did routine translation, was relegated to Rengo, and now studies ceramics in Talagante.
subfiles.title: FBI Memorandum on Isao Takeda (Terashima)

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an investigative memorandum concerning Edwin R. Muller and alleged Japanese espionage correspondence linked to Henri Catherin Gravet in Argentina.
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover - Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards a memo on Edwin Muller and Henri Gravet after Argentine investigation linked Japanese agent Nobuo Ikeda's mail to Muller's Santiago address.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover transmitting memorandum on Henri Catherin Gravet and Edwin R. Muller
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon - Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State

subfiles.about: Investigative report on Edwin R. Muller, the Hotel Pacífico in Algarrobo, and anonymous mail sent from 510 Morandé to Japanese agent Nobuo Ikeda.
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Investigation finds Edwin Muller denies contact with Japanese agent Nobuo Ikeda despite his old Santiago boarding house address appearing on Ikeda's mail; no guest logs existed to confirm who used it.
subfiles.title: FBI Memorandum on Edwin R. Muller and 510 Morandé
